candidates.title: Calgary friends win $90M in country's largest-ever lotto jackpot
candidates.description: A group of four Calgary friends who won the country’s largest-ever lottery jackpot had made their intentions clear with the name of their group chat: Manifesting Millions.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Landslide risk prompts evacuation order for village of Zeballos on Vancouver Island
candidates.description: A state of local emergency and an evacuation order have been issued for Zeballos, a village of about 125 people on the northwest coast of Vancouver Island, due to flooding and potential landslide risks.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Council seat in Norfolk County, Ont., finally decided by a draw out of a top hat
candidates.description: After a long campaign, a recount and two weeks of uncertainty, the race for a Norfolk County council seat was left up to fate. Chris Van Paassen will return as Ward 4 councillor after Norfolk County Clerk William Tigert drew his name from a hat Thursday night, breaking a tie with challenger Jeni Lambert.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: A mysterious U.S. army barrel washed ashore in Quebec. Why did it drum up anthrax concerns?
candidates.description: Quebec provincial police have confirmed that a barrel discovered on an uninhabited island in the St-Lawrence River does not contain active anthrax — ruling out the most dangerous possibility in an ongoing mystery.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: They thought they buried their brother in the family plot; it was a stranger instead
candidates.description: When two sisters from Springdale, N.L., made arrangements to bury their brother, they weren’t prepared for the ordeal ahead. Now, a year later, they’re hoping by sharing their story, it will lead to changes in how cremations are handled in the province.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: First Nation sounds alarm over Ontario proposal to prevent 'obstruction' to development
candidates.description: The Ontario government is considering changes to address what it calls “obstruction” to economic development projects, raising concerns from Neskantaga First Nation about its right to defend its homelands. Here's what we know about the proposal, which one assistant law professor describes as “very vague.”
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Saskatoon mother sentenced for baby's drowning death in bathtub
candidates.description: Melanie O'Soup cried and hung her head in court as lawyers described how her baby died, after she took him into the bath with her and then fell asleep.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Court action halted after clergy therapy centre reveals destruction of records related to abusive priest
candidates.description: The former insurance company for the Catholic church in Newfoundland has abandoned a court action that sought to compel a therapy centre for priests to turn over records after it was revealed they destroyed them more than 20 years ago.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian economy lost 4,700 jobs in October as unemployment rate ticked up to 6.7%
candidates.description: The loss of a few thousand jobs last month follows big back-to-back job losses in August and September, when the Canadian economy shed more than 100,000 roles cumulatively over two months.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: First Nations challenging Pacific Link pipeline’s national-interest designation
candidates.description: Three First Nations in Alberta have filed legal challenges in an attempt to overturn the federal government’s designation of the Pacific Link pipeline as a project in the national interest.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Carney's bet on economic growth — and the risks that come with it
candidates.description: Mark Carney believes he can borrow billions now to invest into major projects and jump start the Canadian economy. If those investments don't pay off, Canada's debt load leaves it exposed to other, new risks.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Alberta becomes 1st province to allow optometrists to perform minor surgeries
candidates.description: As of Nov. 1, Alberta optometrists who undergo further training will be able to perform certain minor surgical procedures.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Owners of homes atop northeastern Ontario gold deposit in shock over a mine that may never be built
candidates.description: A mining company CEO revealed he was considering building an open-pit gold mine right in Virginiatown, Ont., leaving residents of the community of about 500 people in shock. "I do feel frustrated and quite worried," says one homeowner.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Worst of beef price hikes may be over, but don’t expect cheaper steak anytime soon
candidates.description: Beef prices are at record highs. But there is some good news for Canadians who enjoy a good steak. Beef prices have stabilized, but experts say that doesn't mean grocery prices will be dropping anytime soon.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Carney's new budget aims to end homelessness in 10 years
candidates.description: Canada is embarking on a path to end homelessness in 10 years, Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne said as he presented the federal budget on Thursday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: From groceries to tax credits, how much is in the federal budget for your wallet?
candidates.description: The 2026 budget increases payments for the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit, expands a tax credit for low-wage workers and makes the Canada caregiver credit refundable. But the affordability measures are mostly for the short term, and took a back seat to measures aimed at boosting investment.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 15 patients released, 5 still hospitalized following bus crash near Mackenzie, B.C.
candidates.description: WorkSafeBC and RCMP are still investigating what police described as a "chaotic scene" when the shuttle bus went off Highway 39, causing hospitals in Prince George and Mackenzie to declare a code orange.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 7 takeaways from the Carney government's 2nd budget
candidates.description: The 2026 federal budget outlines billions in new spending, but mostly on non-permanent measures. Here are some takeaways.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Republicans ran away from Trump's Canadian tariffs, but not far enough
candidates.description: Several Republicans sought to distance themselves from Donald Trump's trade war during the midterms, in some cases asking for specific tariffs to be rolled back. Even so, Republicans lost. Democrats, who were traditionally the party of protectionism, appear to have been pushed into a more pro-free trade stance, and appear ready to try to reach a deal with Republicans.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What we know about Europe's latest wave of bomb threats targeting flights — and now newsrooms
candidates.description: A spate of bomb threats across Europe has thrown airports and newsrooms into disarray over the past week, forcing flight diversions and emergency landings while prompting broadcast suspensions and evacuations.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Meghan Markle's father arrested and charged with possessing child sexual abuse material
candidates.description: Thomas Markle, the father of Prince Harry's wife, Meghan, was arrested Friday morning by federal agents in Florida on a federal criminal complaint alleging he kept child sexual abuse material, including sexually explicit photographs of himself with prepubescent girls, said the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of California.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Dad of 20-year-old co-pilot in Florida Learjet crash says final radio calls showed 'she's tough'
candidates.description: The father of the 20-year-old co-pilot who died along with eight others when their Learjet crashed in Florida said Friday he has listened to his daughter's heartbreaking final radio transmissions "many times" since the crash.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump's Justice Department hit by 2 high-profile departures this week
candidates.description: Jason Reding Quiñones, who oversaw probes into past criminal investigations of U.S. President Donald Trump as ‌the top federal prosecutor in Miami, has resigned, Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Friday. His departure follows the announcement on Thursday that Harmeet Dhillon was leaving her post leading to the Justice Department's civil rights unit.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: IN PHOTOS | Peru unveils giant statue of Pope Leo ahead of his Latin America visit
candidates.description: Pope Leo XIV is returning home to the continent where he spent two decades as a missionary priest and learned to be a pastor, visiting Uruguay, Argentina and his second homeland of Peru. Here's a look at a tribute to the pontiff by a Peruvian sculptor.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada, others call on China to end 'unjust prosecutions' after sentencing of Joshua Wong
candidates.description: The Canadian government has joined nine other countries in a joint statement condemning this week's prison sentence for Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie sentenced to 200 years in prison for murder of 190 children
candidates.description: A Kenyan court sentenced cult leader Paul Mackenzie on Friday to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children starved to death on his orders and buried in a forest, among 500 suspected victims of one of the worst ceremonial massacres of modern times.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Holocaust survivor, 90, dies nearly a year after being wounded in mass shooting at Australian Hanukkah event
candidates.description: A 90-year-old Holocaust survivor has died almost a year after she was wounded during the massacre of 15 people at a Sydney Hanukkah celebration, officials said Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Death toll from Russian attack in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region climbs to 53
candidates.description: The death toll from Russia's bombing of an aid distribution point in Ukraine's southeastern Zaporizhzhia region on Monday has risen to 53, the acting regional governor said Friday, making it one of the deadliest strikes on civilians this year.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: California Gov. Gavin Newsom says he'll commute all death row sentences to life in prison
candidates.description: California governor Gavin Newsom is commuting the death sentences of more than 500 inmates to life in prison with no parole, saying he believes state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with the values of California, undermines the foundations of the legal system and "diminishes each of us."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: L.A. has a new mayor, and she's a democratic socialist
candidates.description: Nithya Raman, a little-known Los Angeles City Council member backed by the Democratic Socialists of America, has defeated Mayor Karen Bass, an upset that will alter the trajectory of the nation's second-largest city.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Hegseth defends record as Pentagon chief, slams 'sham' push for his impeachment
candidates.description: U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth issued a video message on Thursday vowing to fight efforts in Congress to impeach him and defending the Iran war as "courageous and historic" after voters punished Republicans over it in this week’s midterm elections.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Dolly Parton's manager moves to drop complaint against late singer's nephew
candidates.description: Dolly Parton's longtime manager moved Thursday to drop a complaint that accused the late singer's nephew who acted as her head of security with threatening her estate and its employees.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: AI stock sell-off sends the S&P 500 down 4.4% in worst day since April 2025
candidates.description: AI stocks worldwide felt pressure as worries rise about possible moratoriums on data centres following Democratic victories in the U.S. midterm elections.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Bomb threats affect at least 27 flights, leading to emergency landings at several European airports
candidates.description: A series of hoax ‌bomb threats hit European airlines from Ireland to Bulgaria on Thursday morning for the second time this week, with some of at least 27 affected flights making unplanned landings or being escorted by fighter jets.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Mexican judge arrested over alleged $2M bribe to release Ryan Wedding's second-in-command
candidates.description: A Mexican judge has been arrested on allegations that he accepted a $2-million US bribe in exchange for granting bail to a man accused of acting as second-in-command to Ryan Wedding, the former Canadian Olympic snowboarder turned alleged drug kingpin, American officials said on Thursday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ohio and Texas went from red to blue in the midterms but may not stay that way in 2028
candidates.description: The Democrats flipping governorships and Senate seats in Texas and Ohio turned the states dramatically blue on election night. Some political observers say these wins don't necessarily mean the states will stay that colour, but they do reveal a new political reality — that they'll be electoral battlegrounds in the 2028 presidential election.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Melania Trump hosted officials from Russia and Ukraine. Just what's behind her peace push?
candidates.description: As President Donald Trump and his fellow Republicans take stock after a devastating midterm election that saw the Democrats seize control of Congress, his wife Melania is preparing to host representatives who will almost certainly praise Washington's actions.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Your questions about this year's federal budget, answered
candidates.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney's government unveiled a budget Thursday that covered more than $150 billion in spending, detailed in a 500-plus-page document. As Canadians attempt to parse what the budget means for them, here are answers to some of the questions sent in by CBC readers, viewers and listeners.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: New York Times might buy Letterboxd for $330M US: report
candidates.description: The ​New York Times Company is in exclusive talks to acquire film-focused social platform Letterboxd in a deal valued at about $330 million US, the New York Times reported on Thursday, citing two ‌people familiar with the discussions.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Joly asks Competition Bureau to investigate Cleveland-Cliffs purchase of Stelco
candidates.description: Canada's industry minister is asking the Competition Bureau to investigate Stelco's parent company after its CEO told CBC News that he only bought the Hamilton steelmaker to stop it undercutting his U.S. business.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Tesla will stop making Cybertrucks next year: Musk
candidates.description: Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas Gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk said on Friday, after years of persistently weak sales for a futuristic model once touted as a rival to legacy pickup trucks.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What prediction markets told us about the midterm election
candidates.description: While Kalshi and Polymarket hail big wins for their accurate midterm markets, experts say they missed out on historic and surprise wins.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ottawa readies ban on fees for moving investment accounts
candidates.description: The federal government has released draft regulations to stop banks from charging fees when a client moves an investment account to a different financial institution.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Maple Leaf Foods plans to raise prices again early next year, CEO says in earnings call
candidates.description: Maple Leaf raised prices earlier this year to help offset higher costs — the second such price increase in a year — but it hasn't been enough to mitigate rising expenses.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: CBC Money to launch next year with slate of original content dedicated to personal finance
candidates.description: CBC is announcing the launch of CBC Money, a new slate of original content coming next year that will focus on the daily cost-of-living news that matters to Canadians.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What to watch for as Carney introduces his 2nd federal budget
candidates.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney will deliver his second federal budget on Thursday as the Liberal government reveals next steps in its plan to support the country through an affordability crunch and the trade war.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Is Grand Theft Auto VI the most anticipated video game of all time? Here are some reasons why
candidates.description: The latest in the long-running series of crime simulators by Rockstar Games is predicted to be the biggest release in video game history.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
candidates.description: Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat election victory would mean slower AI development.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people
candidates.description: Paul Mackenzie ordered his followers to starve their children to death in a forest so they could "meet Jesus".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Judge blocks construction of Trump's massive arch after federal agency approval
candidates.description: The Trump administration had hoped the construction of the 250-foot arch could begin as early as this week.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Russian extremist group denies sending hoax bomb threats
candidates.description: Scores of flights across Europe have received bomb threats this week, but no explosives have been found so far.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Dozens of Democrats eyeing 2028 presidential run, says former Obama aide
candidates.description: Jim Messina tells the BBC that after Democrats' midterm victories he's talked to "over two dozen campaigns", with some already hiring staff.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Elon Musk appears to signal the end of the road for Cybertruck
candidates.description: Musk said it was to make room for production of its Cybercabs - autonomous taxis without a driver.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Somalia's top court rejects president's term extension amid political crisis
candidates.description: The country's first nationwide elections since 1969 are due next year - a timetable now thrown into doubt.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Nigerian court rules opposition candidate cannot stand in elections
candidates.description: The high court has sacked the leadership of the opposition ADC party with only months to go until elections.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Macau jails pro-democracy campaigner in city's first national security case
candidates.description: Au Kam San was sentenced to 12 years and six months' jail for "subversion against the political power of the state".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse
candidates.description: The move follows a bank collapse and after the lower house of congress voted in favour of pursuing an impeachment trial against him.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Is it the end of the road for Tesla's Cybertruck?
candidates.description: The car company's CEO Elon Musk has said production will halt in Texas, to focus on the firm's self-driving Cybercabs.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Bomb hoaxes: Messages reveal how threat was passed on by air traffic control
candidates.description: BBC Verify has been analysing messages after flights across Europe were targeted by fake bomb threats - the second such incident this week.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US midterm results spark fears in Israel over future of two countries' ties
candidates.description: Staunch US support of Israel has been raised as one of the reasons why Republicans performed so badly.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: What to know about the presidential wiretapping scandal rocking Indonesia
candidates.description: The scandal involves senior members of President Prabowo Subianto's government, and hint at growing tensions among its elites.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: A wildfire killed their loved ones in Spain. These British families demand to know why
candidates.description: Nine British nationals were among the 15 people who died when fire ripped through the village of Bédar this summer.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US midterm election results?
candidates.description: BBC Verify examines whether US voters were influenced by the data centre boom - and the impact anti-AI sentiment could have on the industry.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff
candidates.description: Fears of more AI regulation appear to have sparked fear among investors, but concerns about the industry have been growing for some time.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Could the earliest weakening of the polar vortex on record bring UK snow?
candidates.description: An unprecedented early weakening of the polar vortex is causing uncertainty amongst experts over the impact it will have on UK weather as Simon King explains.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Typhoons batter East Asia as El Niño makes Pacific 'burn with fever'
candidates.description: Even for countries where typhoons are a way of life, the last few months have brought unusually wild weather.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US rockets firm eyes up mothballed Highland spaceport
candidates.description: Colorado-based Leap is looking at the spaceport near Tongue as its first launch site outside of the US.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Wales scraps controversial Uganda tree-planting scheme
candidates.description: The Welsh government has given more than £4m to the scheme since 2015, but will end it due to budget pressures.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Israel's Arab-led parties in spotlight after inconclusive election
candidates.description: Israel's center-right opposition has a chance to unseat Netanyahu — but backing of Arab-led parties will be key
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Pope Leo begins a 12-day, 3-country South America tour after his cancer surgery
candidates.description: Pope Leo begins his first South American tour since lung cancer surgery. The 12-day journey takes him to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where he spent two decades.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Health intel-sharing group warns industry in wake of cyberattack on French blood bank
candidates.description: A healthcare intelligence-sharing organization is warning its members to lock down systems following cyberattacks on cold storage systems, including a French blood bank.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: European flights and broadcasters are targeted with another wave of bomb threats
candidates.description: Officials across Europe reported a slew of bomb threats against multiple flights, following a string of hoaxes that caused flight diversions this week. Three broadcasters also received threats.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult is sentenced to 200 years in prison
candidates.description: Cult leader Paul Mackenzie was convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult after he ordered his followers to starve themselves to death in order to meet Jesus.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Ex-lawmaker gets 12.5 years in Macao's first national security case
candidates.description: Au's arrest last year was the first publicly known prosecution under Macao's national security law since it was enacted in 2009.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Judge halts construction of Trump's arch. And, Labor Department to release jobs report
candidates.description: A judge has blocked construction of Trump's arch moments after it won federal approval to proceed. And, the Labor Department is set to release the latest jobs report today, a day after stocks plunged.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: After cancer surgery, Pope Leo embarks on Latin America trip
candidates.description: Pope Leo XIV is kicking off a three-nation tour of Latin America with a visit to Uruguay, three weeks after undergoing lung cancer surgery that had put the entire trip into question.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Paraguay's president is impeached minutes after resigning following a bank collapse
candidates.description: Paraguayan lawmakers voted to impeach President Santiago Peña minutes after his resignation, as the collapse of a digital bank tied to his government froze millions of people's savings.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: From comedian to convicted rapist: What to know about Russell Brand
candidates.description: On Monday Brand will learn his sentence, which a judge has warned will likely be 'significant.' It comes after a London jury found him guilty this week on multiple counts of sexual assault and one count of rape.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Hiring jumps: The economy added 165,000 jobs last month
candidates.description: The U.S. job market improved last month, according to a report from the Labor Department Friday. Employers added more jobs than forecasters had expected and the unemployment rate dipped to 4.1%.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Why gold prices are surprisingly low
candidates.description: Gold tends to go up when there's uncertainty in the economy. For a while, the price reflected that. But this week, it dropped from a nearly $5,600 in January to below $4,000. What's going on?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Fears of an AI crackdown after midterms spark $2 trillion rout in tech stocks
candidates.description: Shares sank, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq dropping over 5%, as investors reacted with fear that a Democratic Congress — and states across the country -— would crack down on AI and data centers.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Pasture mealybugs have killed off huge swaths of grasses in the Southeast
candidates.description: An invasive insect that's tough to detect and eliminate poses a multi-billion dollar threat to the agricultural economy — adding another stressor to farmers already stretched by high costs.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: First-time homebuyers remain scarce, but a record share of them pay all cash
candidates.description: A new report finds generational wealth is widening the divide between homebuyers and those priced out. The median age of first-time buyers also remains at a record high.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: As budgets tighten, people are breaking out their library cards
candidates.description: Some Americans squeezed by high prices are relying more on their local libraries for things like books, streaming services and high-priced items like musical instruments and sewing machines.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Does the blue wave mean lower gasoline and diesel prices soon? Don't hold your breath
candidates.description: A new Democratic majority in Congress could pressure the president to end the war in Iran. But it will be harder for them to directly affect fuel prices, which are tied to a complex international oil market.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trump's global health strategy is emerging. What will the Democratic Congress say?
candidates.description: The Trump Administration has ushered in a fundamental shift in the U.S. approach to global health aid. How will the newly elected Democratic Congress weigh in?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Past White House adviser Raj Panjabi has written a playbook for 'living room' crises
candidates.description: Dr. Raj Panjabi is the author of Safer: A Playbook. His goal is to help people face a personal crisis — health, workplace, family conflicts — and "turn fear into action."
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Teens worldwide aren't getting enough exercise -- especially girls
candidates.description: A new study looks at the recommended amount of daily exercise for adolescents — and how few are getting it.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
candidates.description: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. We present SwarmEvolve, a framework in which hundreds of low-cost agents per round work in swarms, reason in latent space without decoding to text, and share information by passing KV caches. Each swarm studies the problem from a different angle. A novelty filter keeps the most distinct agent ideas by directly measuring the distances between the agents' hidden state vectors. Crossover of ideas happens naturally in latent space, as a summarizer agent receives the combined KV caches of all swarm members. On 21 problems in mathematical discovery and scientific computing, SwarmEvolve gets the highest average score and needs a median of only 3 to 8 minutes to reach the best scores that other state-of-the-art frameworks reach in 60 minutes. On several problems, SwarmEvolve with Qwen3 8B improves on the solutions that AlphaEvolve first found with frontier LLMs. Our work shows that agent swarms that communicate in latent space offer a fast, low-cost approach to program search for scientific problems.
candidates.author: Qile Jiang, George Em Karniadakis

candidates.title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
candidates.description: AI-Scientists arrived, but a world for them to grow in did not. Human scientists take theirs for granted $-$ centuries of open problems and shared ideas, waiting in the scientific literature. To AI-Scientists, that world is readable but not runnable, so we build Scientist World for them: every research paper becomes an executable environment. Our autonomous pipeline extracts each paper's open-ended research question and reproduces its proposed method as the baseline; an AI-Scientist entering the environment is evaluated against what the human authors achieved. We release the first 1,000 verified environments. With the world as an evaluation, we found that frontier AI-Scientists can already surpass the human researchers 74% of the time. As a record of how AI does science, it contains 6,400 hours of research traces, with every idea, experiment, failure, and success. As a training ground, we are able to raise (+158%) a small model to match frontier models in research ideation. At last, AI-Scientists' own world has arrived, grown from and growing with science itself.
candidates.author: Taiming Lu, Sachin Konan, Zhuang Liu

candidates.title: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration
candidates.description: ML code should run where researchers choose, not where it was first written. Today, machine learning code mainly lives in two ecosystems, PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs and JAX on Google TPUs. Migrating repositories between them means building and testing across frameworks and hardware. This migration is (1) a practical need, since it unlocks different hardware for researchers, and (2) a natural benchmark: it involves different frameworks and hardware, covers whole repositories, and is long-horizon and challenging. We introduce XStack, a benchmark that evaluates agents on migrating ML repositories between these two ecosystems. Each agent receives a PyTorch repository and a clean TPU machine and must deliver a JAX repository. Its output passes if it meets our grading criteria, based on the source repository's published result, authenticated and calibrated by us. Migration by agents remains unreliable: Claude Opus 5 passes 75%, GPT-5.6-sol 45%, and every other agent at most 40%. XStack is a step toward freeing ML code from its ecosystem. We release XStack to make progress toward reliable migration across frameworks and hardware measurable.
candidates.author: Linrong Cai, Taiming Lu, Haozhe Chen, Zhuang Liu

candidates.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
candidates.description: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions. We ask when such a quantity is identifiable from an experiment's access, continuous in the mechanism and certifiable from finite data, and answer exactly for a deliberately demanding case - the integrated information $\varphi$ of integrated information theory - in stochastic networks of four and five units with known ground truth. Behavior can be silent: a recurrent and a feed-forward network with identical input-output laws at their response delay carry 0.28 and 0 bits, yet internal recordings separate them within 4-53 trials. Partial access can be just as blind: in our examples, units left out of a one-step recording impose precision floors of 0.30-1.02 bits that no sample size lowers, and in all-but-self parity networks, recordings of any length see several hidden units only through the product of their fidelities - a symmetry that one intervention broke in exact checks. The measure has sharp edges: because $\varphi$ selects a partition, and the cause and effect it specifies, by one criterion and reports another, infinitesimal changes of mechanism that cross an edge change it by 25-100% at 99% of the edges we found in random networks, and about 1% of surrogate models that fit interventional data almost perfectly misreport it by more than 20%. One-sided claims survive: the same data certify a lower bound on both sides of an edge, and we prove $\varphi>1.004$ bits throughout a 64-dimensional region of mechanisms and certify it from about $10^7$ controlled transitions with false-certificate probability at most $α$. Measurability is thus a design question with computable answers.
candidates.author: Linqian Wu, Diaoxuan He

candidates.title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
candidates.description: To interpret a direction in a language model's residual stream, we can look for text that strongly activates it. But when such text is found by scanning a corpus, it is limited to what that corpus contains. We develop Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs), language models which map residual stream directions from a subject model to text exemplars that strongly activate those directions. Our objective is to maximise the cosine similarity of a supplied residual stream direction with the activations of the text generated by the MAEM. This label-free RL objective helps to scale MAEMs on diverse sources of residual stream directions. Empirically, we find the resultant metamodel produces informative exemplars: a Qwen3.6-27B MAEM inverts held-out activations better than corpus search or a natural-language autoencoder (NLA), beats corpus search (at 10M tokens) on a majority of held-out languages/domains, and activates 89% of held-out SAE features. It also identifies concepts behind steering vectors about as well as NLAs, recovers the payloads of LoRA backdoors more often than corpus search, and can even verbalise some model workspace inner monologue. Unlike explanations produced by other metamodels (e.g. NLAs), MAEM exemplars can be verified with a forward pass on the subject model, making the MAEM objective a grounded alternative for scaling the training of metamodels.
candidates.author: Celeste De Schamphelaere, Juan J. Vazquez, Ari Spiesberger, Tomáš Gavenčiak, Gavin Leech, Euan Ong, Jiahai Feng

candidates.title: OopsieRecover: Learning Transferable VLA Corrections from Semantic Interventions
candidates.description: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform a wide range of robotic manipulation tasks, but often fail during deployment. Teaching them to recover from these failures requires substantial corrective data: existing approaches learn to recover from failures by directly associating corrective actions with the observations in which they were demonstrated. For instance, DAgger-like fine-tuning can require tens to hundreds of interactions, yet the resulting policy may still fail to generalize the learned corrections beyond the demonstrated scenarios. We hypothesize that semantics can capture the underlying reasons for failures and their corrections, enabling policies to learn from only a handful of corrective demonstrations and generalize those corrections to novel objects, and scene variations. We propose OopsieRecover, a framework that uses abduction to infer the intent behind a small set of corrective demonstrations and encodes the inferred knowledge as dense spatial representations and conditional costs. These costs capture when a behavior is undesirable and steer the policy toward more desirable action regions. We experiment across 6 tasks and variations in object poses, scenes, and related tasks, and find that only a handful of corrective demonstrations can enable a VLA to overcome failures across a broad range of novel situations, without requiring new corrective data for each variation. Please refer to https://robin-lab.cs.utexas.edu/oopsierecover for videos.
candidates.author: Arpit Bahety, Skand Peri, Sriniket Ambatipudi, Chen Xu, Haruki Nishimura, Masha Itkina, Roberto Martín-Martín

candidates.title: Latent RL Priors for Data-Efficient Dexterous Manipulation
candidates.description: Learning dexterous manipulation from limited visual demonstrations is challenging because policies must acquire both perceptual grounding and precise control, while reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation can acquire rich control behaviors from large-scale interaction with privileged information. We introduce \textbf{Latent RL Prior}, a two-stage framework that reuses this control knowledge for data-efficient visual policy learning. During privileged pretraining, we distill large-scale RL rollouts into a flow-matching action decoder conditioned on proprioception and latent task context. During visual adaptation, we freeze the decoder and learn a visual interface that maps images to its latent context using action supervision alone, without privileged labels or latent targets. The same decoder can further be shared across arms by learning coordinated visual contexts for bimanual manipulation. Across three simulated tasks, our method outperforms full-parameter fine-tuning of $π_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.7 in the low-data regime; on door lifting and bimanual assembly, it surpasses full-data baselines using $10\times$ and $5\times$ fewer demonstrations, respectively. Further analysis shows that direct visual-to-latent conditioning improves adaptation performance and training stability over routing visual predictions through the pretrained state encoder. Robustness to unseen mass variation and greater linear accessibility of contact-force information in decoder representations further provide evidence of retained RL-acquired control knowledge. Project website: https://yixiaowang7.github.io/latent-rl-prior-page/.
candidates.author: Yixiao Wang, Peiyi Chen, Mustafa Mukadam, Shreekant Gayaka, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Son Tran

candidates.title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
candidates.description: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher's per-token supervision. Does this dense signal reduce the training FLOPs needed to reach a target accuracy compared with reinforcement learning? We systematically compare vanilla reverse-KL OPD with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) across task difficulty, student and teacher size, domain, and optimization choices, measuring held-out accuracy against training FLOPs. With an external post-trained teacher, OPD generally loses to GRPO in accuracy per training FLOP at matched settings, even when the teacher is further trained with GRPO, and often suffers response-length inflation. Yet a different teacher changes the picture: when the teacher is the student's own GRPO checkpoint, OPD recovers that checkpoint's accuracy on math with $50\times$ fewer distillation FLOPs than GRPO needs to reach the same accuracy. Following the same teacher setting, we consistently observe this high efficiency with a larger student, on code, and in a second model family. On a single domain, however, the GRPO checkpoint is already the desired model, so distilling it adds to total compute. Across domains, separate GRPO checkpoints hold different capabilities, and no single checkpoint serves every domain. Multi-teacher OPD (DeepSeek-AI, 2026) consolidates per-domain GRPO experts into a single student that matches each expert's accuracy, with the distillation stage costing only 5.2% (on 2 domains) and 8.0% (on 4 domains) of the specialist training FLOPs. Counting specialist training and distillation together, this pipeline reaches joint GRPO's performance on the 2-domain mix with 42.0% fewer total FLOPs.
candidates.author: Zeyu Leo Liu, Yang Li, Bo Pang, Emre Can Acikgoz, Xuan-Phi Nguyen, Anurag Koul, Srijan Bansal, Erik Nijkamp, Shafiq Joty, Semih Yavuz

candidates.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
candidates.description: Reproducing machine learning experiments requires reconstructing procedures from information scattered across papers, released code, and supporting artifacts. For coding agents, reproduction success can therefore depend on their ability to fill in missing details, rather than on the released artifacts alone. We ask whether preserving recovered procedures and decisions improves subsequent independent reproduction. We define a standardized artifact design comprising a refined codebase, environment setup, experiment launchers, and a reproduction guide, and introduce ReproBridge, an agent workflow for constructing these refined reproducible artifacts. ReproBridge-Bench provides 1,029 tasks from 387 experiments across 36 papers, anchored by five human-verified reference scores per task. Agents attempt tasks in fresh sessions with raw code or refined artifacts; a separate Auditor checks execution evidence. Across four evaluated models, refined artifacts raise mean reproduction success from 76.4% to 92.6% and reduce downstream API spending by 19.7% on average. The cross-model success-rate spread narrows from 21.6 to 3.9 percentage points, with all four models achieving mean success rates above 90%. Removing any component reduces success in the ablation study, with the largest losses from code and environment removal. These results suggest that preserving execution knowledge helps even models with lower raw-code success reproduce experiments more reliably and at lower API cost.
candidates.author: Yubo Wang, Rui Meng, Jaehyun Nam, Tomas Pfister, Jinsung Yoon

candidates.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
candidates.description: Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion. However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. We introduce VFlash, a method for fast, accurate visual planning through Flash Primitive Decoding. VFlash exploits the known structure of visual primitives to predict their coordinates jointly, using a lightweight drafter that generates an entire primitive in one forward pass. The layout adapts to the primitive's type, dimensionality, and length, supporting compact boxes and long, variable-length trajectories. Crucially, spatial accuracy need not require reproducing an autoregressive model's exact token sequence. VFlash therefore trains on annotated primitives and directly accepts structurally valid predictions without target-token agreement. Across the evaluated 2D and 3D robot trajectory tasks, VFlash consistently reduces prediction errors relative to autoregressive decoding. Preliminary single-rollout measurements indicate approximately 25x faster generation for 3D point motion forecasting. A world action model conditioned on VFlash plans achieves 70.2% average success across four MolmoSpaces task suites, compared with 62.6% for the baseline.
candidates.author: Yu-Cheng Chou, Shihao Wang, Jin Huang, Chi-Pin Huang, Chiao-An Yang, Xianzhe Fan, Jing Wang, Zhiqi Li, Yuanguo Kuang, Ruijie Zheng, Johan Bjorck, Sifei Liu, Hang Su, Abhishek Badki, Lei Zhang, Alan Yuille, Linxi "Jim'' Fan, Jan Kautz, Zhiding Yu

candidates.title: Label-Wording Augmentation in a Typed-Decision Encoder: Gains on Unfamiliar Words, Not on Abbreviations or Codes
candidates.description: Typed-decision models score options that the caller supplies at request time, so their accuracy depends on label wording that the model's developer does not control. We compare two releases of a 307M-parameter multilingual cross-encoder, Ru-Jev, trained on thirteen Russian-language tasks; the later release adds an augmentation that presents labels in several surface forms. Holding questions fixed and varying only how eighteen routing labels are worded, we evaluate ten label vocabularies, produced by three separate processes and checked for overlap with the training data, with five candidates per question and, for eight of them, also with eighteen. On held-out vocabularies made of ordinary or borrowed words (English-derived jargon, office slang, department names), the augmented release is more accurate in every setting, by up to 0.24. Eleven of these fourteen gains survive a Holm correction (slang with eighteen candidates and descriptive sentences with five do not), and for jargon on all labels the label-level interval excludes zero in both settings. On abbreviations and opaque codes it gives no usable gain: on abbreviations it is not better, and worse on the clean slice, and on opaque codes both releases stay at or below chance once labels related to training options are removed. In most cells where accuracy rises, the risk-coverage area falls, but with eighteen candidates confident errors rise on jargon and slang. On two datasets neither release saw, accuracy moves by -8.4 and +5.6 points. We also report four evaluation hazards from comparing the two releases.
candidates.author: Vladimir Beskorovainyi

candidates.title: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
candidates.description: Neural networks are likely to be among the most consequential artefacts in human history. As these systems become more capable and autonomous, their potential to cause societal harm also grows, making AI safety one of the defining challenges of our time. Yet we continue to build increasingly powerful systems without fully understanding how they work, how they will behave in unfamiliar situations, or how to reliably control them. Mechanistic interpretability offers a path towards understanding these systems by studying their internal representations and computations, with the aim of evaluating, predicting, and controlling behaviour. We survey mechanistic interpretability for AI safety in order to answer the question: Does understanding how models work actually make them safer? We place mechanistic interpretability in the broader context of interpretability research and compare its mechanistic evidence with behavioural evaluation. We introduce the foundations of mechanistic interpretability, including features, polysemanticity, transformer computation, and circuits, and survey methods for feature extraction and analysis, circuit discovery and causal verification, explaining intermediate representations in natural language, learning dynamics, and training-data attribution. Beyond surveying existing methods, we propose a unified framework for evaluating mechanistic interpretability claims and characterise six research orientations by their goals, assumptions, and trade-offs. Finally, we examine how mechanistic understanding can support AI safety, including knowledge editing, steering, and monitoring, and assess its limitations, failure modes, open problems, and relationship to behavioural safety measures. We also release a repository of code notebooks with worked examples that reproduce key findings from surveyed methods, allowing readers to build intuition through hands-on experimentation.
candidates.author: Fazl Barez, Tung-Yu Wu, Hunar Batra, Gabriele Dominici, Florent Draye, Yanai Elazar, Damiano Fornasiere, Antía García, Abir Harrasse, Riley Harris, Sara Hooker, Michael Lan, Belinda Z.
